about: Synthetic cases for run_checks.py. Each case runs once per provider. A case with schema_from reuses the schema its schema case generated for the same provider; when that case failed, the dependent case is skipped. Values in expect are compared after normalising case, spaces, number formats and dates (see compare_value in run_checks.py).

cases.title: Flat invoice schema keeps date, number and enum types (Finnish task)
cases.requirements: Poimi laskusta nämä kentät. Käytä täsmälleen näitä kenttänimiä: invoice_number (laskun numero, teksti), invoice_date (laskun päivämäärä, päivämäärä muodossa VVVV-KK-PP), supplier (toimittajan nimi, teksti), total_amount (laskun loppusumma veroineen, desimaaliluku), currency (valuutta, yksi arvoista EUR, USD tai SEK).
cases.rubric: Five fields with exactly the requested names. invoice_date is a date in YYYY-MM-DD, total_amount a number, currency limited to EUR, USD and SEK. Descriptions say what each field holds; nothing is added or dropped.

cases.title: Invoice header with a nested list of line items
cases.requirements: Poimi laskun otsikkotiedot ja jokainen laskurivi. Otsikkotiedot: invoice_number (laskun numero, teksti) ja supplier (toimittajan nimi, teksti). Laskurivit listana nimeltä line_items; jokaisella rivillä description (rivin kuvaus, teksti), quantity (määrä, kokonaisluku), unit_price (yksikköhinta, desimaaliluku) ja line_total (rivin summa, desimaaliluku).
cases.rubric: A parent record with invoice_number and supplier, and a list called line_items whose items have description (text), quantity (integer), unit_price and line_total (numbers). The line items are not flattened into the parent.

cases.title: A document that is only a list of records (nested_list) with a choice field
cases.requirements: Extract every inventory item mentioned in the document and return them as a list called inventory_items. Use exactly these field names. For each item, return product_name (the product name, text), quantity (the quantity in stock, an integer), unit_price (the price of one unit, a decimal number) and category (one of: tools, spare_parts, consumables). Create a separate list entry for every distinct product.
cases.rubric: A list called inventory_items and nothing else at the top level: no header fields. Each item has exactly product_name (text), quantity (integer), unit_price (a number) and category limited to tools, spare_parts and consumables.

cases.title: Meeting minutes: header fields and two separate child lists
cases.requirements: Extract structured information from meeting minutes. Use exactly these field names. Return meeting_title (the title of the meeting, text) and meeting_date (the date of the meeting, a date). Return a list called participants with one entry for each participant: name (the participant's name, text) and role (their role in the meeting, text). Also return a separate list called action_items with one entry for each action item: task (what is to be done, text), owner (the person responsible, text) and due_date (the deadline, a date).
cases.rubric: A parent with exactly meeting_title (text) and meeting_date (date), and two separate lists: participants with name and role, and action_items with task, owner and due_date (a date). Neither list is merged into the other or flattened into the parent.

cases.title: Flat schema with a boolean, a whole number, a DD.MM.YYYY date, a list of texts and a stated default
cases.requirements:
Extract the following from a machine inspection report. Use exactly these field names:
- machine_id (the machine's identifier, text)
- has_defects (boolean: true if any defects were found, otherwise false)
- defect_count (the number of defects found, a whole number)
- inspection_date (the date of the inspection, in the format DD.MM.YYYY)
- checked_parts (the parts that were checked, a list of texts)
- inspector_comment (the inspector's comment, text; if no comment is given, return "not given")
cases.rubric: Six fields with exactly the requested names: has_defects a boolean, defect_count an integer, inspection_date a date written as DD.MM.YYYY, checked_parts a list of texts (not a nested list of records), and inspector_comment text whose stated default is "not given".

cases.title: Text extraction from a Finnish invoice (Finnish date and decimal comma)
cases.rubric: One record. total_amount is the total including VAT (551,57), not the net 439,50 or the VAT 112,07. invoice_date is the invoice date 14.3.2026, not the due date 28.3.2026.

cases.title: Two documents in two languages give two records in order
cases.rubric: Two records, the Finnish invoice first. The English invoice's '2 April 2026' becomes 2026-04-02 and '1,250.00' becomes 1250. No value of one document appears in the other's record.

cases.title: Line items from the invoice text into the nested schema
cases.rubric: Exactly three line items in the invoice's order with their own quantities and prices. The net total, VAT and total rows are not line items.

cases.title: Vision extraction from the PDF invoice
cases.rubric: Same values as the text case: total including VAT 551,57 and the invoice date 14.3.2026, read from the page image.

cases.title: Vision extraction from a scanned (PNG) invoice
cases.rubric: Same values as the PDF case, from an image with no text layer.

cases.title: Vision extraction of line items from the PDF
cases.rubric: Three line items read from the page, same as the text case.

cases.title: RAG over both invoices answers from the right one and cites it
cases.question: What is the total including VAT of invoice INV-2026-0042?
cases.rubric: The answer gives 551,57 EUR, the Finnish invoice's total including VAT, not its net 439,50, its VAT 112,07 or the English invoice's 1,250.00. It cites invoice-fi.txt in the form [document_name, page X] and cites no document it did not use.

cases.title: The tabular agent sums one invoice's lines in a CSV
cases.question: What is the sum of line_total for invoice INV-2026-0042?
cases.rubric: The SQL keeps the three lines of INV-2026-0042 and sums their line_total (300.00 + 94.50 + 45.00 = 439.50); the other invoices' lines are not counted. The answer states 439.50.

cases.title: The vision parser turns the PDF invoice into markdown
cases.rubric: Markdown that keeps the page's text: the invoice number INV-2026-0042 (the fixed check reads a typographic dash as a hyphen; report one as a defect), the supplier Esimerkki Oy, the three line items with their quantities and prices (a table is fine), and the totals 439,50, 112,07 and 551,57. Nothing is invented or left out.
